utility.notes: Glendale Water and Power is the City of Glendale's own municipal electric utility. Glendale is notably absent from SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (which lists many neighboring LA County cities but not Glendale), consistent with Glendale having its own municipal utility rather than SCE service. glendaleca.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session, so specific program pages could not be independently read, but GWP's identity and role as the electric utility is corroborated by multiple independent search-engine-indexed GWP program page titles on the city's own domain.

value.name: Glendale Water and Power (GWP)
value.notes: GWP is a vertically-integrated municipal utility (like LADWP, Pasadena Water and Power, and Burbank Water and Power) — it generates/procures and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA. No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Glendale in the sources reviewed this session.

permit_authority.value: City of Glendale Building & Safety, in coordination with Glendale Water and Power
permit_authority.notes: Directly re-verified via browser this session (an earlier HTTP 403 to automated fetch was intermittent, not a persistent block); the full page text was read.

permit_url.notes: Directly re-verified via browser this session; a detailed 12-step process guide.

interconnection_url.notes: Directly re-verified via browser this session — the same 'Guide for Applying for PV Interconnection and NEM' page directly and comprehensively covers GWP's own interconnection/NEM process (PowerClerk application, Interconnection Agreement, GWP meter reprogramming), so is used for both permit_url and interconnection_url. An earlier, differently-titled 'guide-for-applying-for-interconnection' URL identified via search-engine indexing could not be independently confirmed to still exist and is no longer used.

battery_programs.notes: The statewide SGIP program (administered by the CPUC-regulated IOUs) is not applicable to Glendale, since GWP is a municipal utility outside SGIP's administering IOUs' territories. No GWP-specific battery incentive program was confirmed this session.

value.name: PV Interconnection Application (+ optional Energy Storage), submitted via PowerClerk
Full Plan Set (equipment data sheets, photos of existing main service panel, clearances, 3x3 working space)
Shading Analysis Report (waived for PV systems up to 10 kW CEC-AC, subject to a disclosure statement)
Data Sheet for Energy Storage Device

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Guide for Applying for PV Interconnection and NEM for under 15 kW CEC-AC residential systems,' Step 1(a)-(f).

value: After installation, the solar contractor uses their Glendale Permits account to schedule the inspection with Building & Safety
After the inspection and final sign-off, Building & Safety notifies GWP Engineering that the system passed inspection
GWP Engineering then submits a work order to GWP Field Services for NEM reprogramming of the electric meter, taking 7-10 working days
Once the meter is reprogrammed, GWP notifies the contractor/customer that the system can be turned on
inspection_steps.notes: Per the City's own process guide, Steps 9-12.

value.notes: The City's own guide states: 'The GWP Solar Team typically completes the initial review of your PV Interconnection Application (and optional energy storage) within 3-5 business days. This review occurs before your application moves on to Engineering, Building & Safety, or both.' This covers only GWP's own initial interconnection-application review stage (Step 2 of 12); it does not include the separate Building & Safety plan review/permit issuance time (Steps 4-7) or the post-inspection NEM meter reprogramming time (7-10 working days, Step 11), which are not given as day-count figures in this guide.

value.program_or_pathway: PV Interconnection and Net Energy Metering (NEM) for under 15 kW CEC-AC residential systems
other_conditions: PV systems sized up to 10 kW CEC-AC: self-certification of system-size need is accepted within the PowerClerk application, and the Shading Analysis Report is waived (subject to a disclosure statement about nearby trees under 50 feet)
PV systems over 10 kW CEC-AC: GWP uses 110% of the customer's trailing 12-month kWh usage to establish anticipated annual load, compared against PowerClerk's estimated system production
Proposed system size must be primarily intended to offset part or all of the customer's own electrical requirements

permit_fees.notes: The City's guide states Building and Safety 'contacts the solar contractor for payment of fees, issuance of permit, etc.' but does not itself state a dollar amount.
